title: Radar/RF sensor site marker
description: Shared, loosely-typed convention for a fixed sensor site marker, deliberately not one fixed producer's schema: protocols/vendors/asterix/cat.py's CAT-34 handler and protocols/vendors/aartos/aartos_json.py's antenna_to_site() both publish this shape (with different optional fields) to '{TOPIC_ROOT}/land/*/radar/neutral/radar/**', which layers/tak_layer.py's dedicated radar-status subscriber renders generically (reading only the plain JSON view either way). A new sensor integration matching these field names renders with zero tak_layer.py changes. NOT a shared rule on the dual-view question: cat.py's CAT-34 site marker also goes through publish_dual() (SAPIENT+protobuf, same as every other CAT-34 message) — this schema documents its JSON leg. aartos_json.py's site marker is the one that deliberately skips publish_dual entirely (its own comment: 'no dual protobuf view for this one... there is no per-vendor schema for this') and is bare-JSON-only, unlike its own main per-track record which does go through publish_dual.

uid.description: Object id; falls back to sensor_id when absent (track_views' object_id() checks uid first).

sensor_type.description: Present on CAT-34 ('radar'); absent on AARTOS.

passive.description: true for a receive-only system (VERA-NG, AARTOS IsoLOG) — rendered with the Direction Finding icon, not the emitting-radar one.

radar_clock_s.description: CAT-34 only (from the ASTERIX record's own tod_s).

speed_ms.description: CAT-34 only — the site's own platform speed, when mobile.
